source: Russek et al. (2017) Predictive representations can link model-based RL to model-free mechanisms
finding: Grid-world simulations separate five learners on three revaluation tests. SR-Dyna passes reward, transition and policy revaluation if replay is enough. SR-TD passes only reward revaluation.
numbers: SR-TD: reward pass, detour fail, policy fail. SR-MB: reward pass, detour pass, novel-policy fail. SR-Dyna: all pass with enough replay (policy test used 10,000 replayed samples). Depth-limited model-free TD fails all three.
limits: Simulation only, no new human data. Uniform replay scheme. Tabular, S^2 memory for the successor matrix.
agent_relevance: Offline replay of stored subgoal links can give flexible updates without search at decision time, but only if the replay budget is large enough.

source: Russek et al. (2017) failure modes of the models
finding: Failures are parameter-independent: a model that fails a test cannot be rescued by tuning. With sparse replay SR-Dyna decays to SR-TD (reward revaluation only). Dyna-Q with too little replay fails all three tests.
numbers: SR-Dyna with little replay: reward pass, transition fail, policy fail. Dyna-Q with little replay: fails all 3.
limits: Qualitative pass/fail in simulation.
agent_relevance: Replay budget is a hard dial. Too little replay looks updated for easy changes and stale for structural ones.

source: Russek et al. (2017) discriminating predictions and open problems
finding: Authors say SR-Dyna cannot yet handle hidden state, and that evaluating novel options with semantic knowledge needs choice-time computation. They propose replay manipulations crossed with the three revaluation types, and rest or distractor manipulations in humans.
numbers: Distractor at decision time reportedly no effect on reward revaluation (fits SR-Dyna). Extra pre-decision time helps policy-revaluation-like tasks (fits Dyna-Q and SR-Dyna).
limits: Predictions, not tests. Neural substrate (hippocampus vs prefrontal-striatal SR) left open.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on replay for novel-option evaluation. Keep a live search step for that.

source: Momennejad et al. (2017) The successor representation in human reinforcement learning (bioRxiv preprint), Experiment 1
finding: People revalue reward changes better than transition changes. Pure SR and pure model-based both mispredict this asymmetry; a hybrid SR-MB fit both experiments.
numbers: N=58 analysed (69 recruited). Revaluation score: reward .520, transition .450, control .031. Reward vs transition t(57)=2.89, p<.01. Control vs 0 t(57)=1.2, p=.22. Transition RT slower t(57)=2.08.
limits: This is the preprint. The published version is cited by later work as best fit by SR-Dyna; I could not read the published text. The preprint gives no numeric fit statistics.
agent_relevance: Humans are worse at structural updates than value updates. An agent that treats them equally is not humanlike and may be miscalibrated.

source: Momennejad et al. (2017) Experiment 2 (active task, MTurk)
finding: Proportion switching stage-1 choice after change: reward .66, policy .50, transition .47, control .08. Policy revaluation patterned with transition revaluation.
numbers: N=88 analysed (112 recruited). Reward vs transition Wald Z=-2.85, p=.0034. Reward vs policy Z=-2.61, p=.0043. Policy vs transition Z=0.56, p=.58.
limits: Online sample. The gap is about 0.2 in proportion.
agent_relevance: Cheap value edits propagate; structural edits need an extra mechanism.

source: Momennejad (2020) Learning structures: predictive representations, replay, and generalization
finding: Review states human revaluation was best captured by SR-Dyna, beating MF, MB, MF-MB, Dyna-Q(+), prioritised Dyna and SR without replay, citing Russek 2017 and Momennejad 2017.
numbers: No new numbers. Table 1 caveats: Dyna-Q cannot find new shortcuts; Dyna-Q+ needs many samples; prioritised sweeping struggles with large decision trees; SR-Dyna limited to discrete states.
limits: Review, so the best-fit claim rests on two studies, one of them simulation. Model comparison depends on small two-stage tasks.
agent_relevance: Source of the headline claim for this subfield; treat as medium strength, not settled.

source: Momennejad (2020) boundary conditions of SR
finding: TD-learned SR stops converging to the random-walk SR when rewards are non-uniform, obstacles exist or visits are uneven. A short-horizon SR (gamma 0.1) misses relations between distant states.
numbers: Bistro problem: gamma=.1 fails to relate states 2 and 8.
limits: Illustrative toy cases.
agent_relevance: A library of subgoal links built from experienced visits will be biased toward the visited path (policy-dependent).

source: Momennejad, Otto, Daw and Norman (2018) Offline replay supports planning in human reinforcement learning (eLife)
finding: fMRI two-stage task: replay of stage-1 categories during rest predicted later replanning after revaluation, not after control.
numbers: N=24 analysed (26 recruited). Replanning: revaluation t(23)=4.89 p<.0001; control t(23)=-0.10 p=.92. Replay-replanning Spearman rho=.54 p=.0068 (revaluation) vs rho=-.13 p=.55 (control); difference p=.023.
limits: Correlational. Stage-2 replay control not significant (rho .2, p .17). Rest1 vs Rest3 correlation difference not significant (p=.31). Small N.
agent_relevance: Direct human support that offline reactivation relates to later updating, but only a correlation.

source: Momennejad et al. (2018) noise and prediction-error moderators
finding: Unsigned prediction errors predicted later replay and replanning in ACC, precuneus and putamen. The replay-behaviour link appeared mainly in noisy-reward blocks.
numbers: Revaluation vs control in noisy blocks p=.066; noiseless p=.16; interaction p=.34 (not significant). Rest-1 replay higher in revaluation blocks t(23)=2.17 p=.039; replay falls Rest1 to Rest3 t(23)=2.9 p=.007. Left hippocampus Z=4.74.
limits: The noise-by-revaluation interaction was null. Noiseless blocks had low replay (possible ceiling).
agent_relevance: Prioritise replay of items with large surprise; supports surprise-triggered rather than scheduled revision (fits G1).

source: Liu, Dolan, Kurth-Nelson and Behrens (2019) Human replay spontaneously reorganizes experience (Cell)
finding: MEG shows replay in rest that follows the learned rule order, not the seen order, and reverses after reward. Replay can transfer structure to objects never seen.
numbers: Study1 N=21 analysed: forward beta=.017+-.005 at 40 ms (16/21). Reverse after reward beta=-.028+-.010; rewarded sequence -.052+-.018. Study2 N=22: forward .021+-.009 (17/22). Transfer replay beta=-.036+-.008.
limits: About 20 per study. MEG source localisation is imprecise. Replay strength did not correlate with performance (possible ceiling). Origin of pre-experience sequences unresolved.
agent_relevance: Replay is not a copy of experience: it recombines by abstract structure. An offline pass might reorder subgoals by a learned rule.

source: Gillespie et al. (2021) Hippocampal replay reflects specific past experiences rather than a plan for subsequent choice (Neuron)
finding: Rat CA1 replay in an eight-arm task favoured the previous goal arm and long-unvisited arms. It did not predict the next choice. The authors argue replay serves memory maintenance, a challenge to the planning reading of Dyna.
numbers: 4 rats. Remote replay 35.1, 41.1, 34.5, 47.2% of ripples. About 20% of pre-choice remote events for the previous goal arm, about 2-fold over baseline. Upcoming-arm replay significant in 2/4 (subset) or 3/4 (GLM). Classifier from replay counts near chance. Previous-goal replay vs later visits p=.08-.49.
limits: Four animals, one task. No ripple disruption in this paper. Weak R2 (.012-.033) for current-goal replay.
agent_relevance: Failed-prediction evidence: replay need not choose the next action. Offline pass may be best seen as library upkeep, which is our use.

source: Gillespie et al. (2021) literature framing (bioRxiv version)
finding: Intro lists the pro-planning evidence: replay of the path about to be taken (Pfeiffer and Foster 2013; Xu 2019), hippocampal-prefrontal coordination (Shin 2019), replay of aversive paths before avoidance (Wu 2017). Disruption studies (Jadhav 2012; Nokia 2012; Fernandez-Ruiz 2019) show learning effects.
numbers: No numbers. Named citations only.
limits: The cited studies were not opened by me.
agent_relevance: Follow-up reading: Jadhav 2012 and Fernandez-Ruiz 2019 for causal tests.

source: Tomov, Schulz and Gershman (2019/2021) Multi-task reinforcement learning in humans
finding: People reusing old policies for a new reward function chose the successor-feature plus GPI prediction more than the model-based or model-free prediction in 3 of 4 experiments. Experiment 4 was preregistered.
numbers: Exp1 N=132: SF&GPI 26 (p=.003), MB 33. Exp2 N=96: 30 vs 7. Exp3 N=113: 32 vs 8. Exp4 N=303 (500 recruited): 81 (p=4.4e-14) vs 46 (p=.02, BF=1.8); BF=22.4 favouring SF&GPI over MB. About 40% excluded for low training reward.
limits: Heavy exclusion (about 40%). Experiment 1 showed no difference between SF&GPI and model-based. Tabular deterministic task. SF&GPI is not SR-Dyna.
agent_relevance: Independent preregistered support for the predictive-reuse family, though not for replay itself.

source: Stachenfeld et al. (2017), Garvert et al. (2017), Schapiro et al. (2013) as cited in Momennejad 2020
finding: Cited as SR-consistent evidence: place and grid fields, fMRI pattern similarity in association learning and community-structure learning.
numbers: Not given in review.
limits: Seen only through the review; not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports the representation, not the replay mechanism.

source: Sarel et al. (2017), Boccara et al. (2019), Butler et al. (2019) as cited in Momennejad 2020
finding: Bat goal-vector cells bend around obstacles and grid fields shift toward reward; read as policy-dependent SR.
numbers: Not given in review.
limits: Seen only through the review; not opened.
agent_relevance: Policy dependence is seen in animals too.

source: Momennejad (2020) summary of the replay-variance finding
finding: Review says the replay-revaluation link was stronger under higher reward variance. The primary paper shows only a trend, with the interaction not significant.
numbers: Review: stronger under high variance. Primary (b09): interaction p=.34.
limits: The review overstates the primary result. Use the primary numbers.
agent_relevance: Do not build a rule on noise-gated replay.

source: Dyna-Mind (2025) Learning to Simulate from Experience for Better AI Agents: Dyna-GRPO
finding: Two stages: ReSim (reasoning traces from search over real interaction) then Dyna-GRPO (online RL with real rollouts). Dyna-GRPO beat plain GRPO on all three benchmarks.
numbers: Dyna-GRPO vs GRPO average success: Sokoban 77.1 vs 73.1, ALFWorld 90.8 vs 87.0, AndroidWorld 31.8 vs 27.8 (3 runs, mean+-std).
limits: Gains are 4 points, near the std on some splits. Needs a trained 7B-32B model, not scaffold-only.
agent_relevance: Closest AI test of Dyna style; gain from simulation-as-training is modest and needs weights.

source: Dyna-Mind (2025) ReSim vs frontier models
finding: Searching a simulated tree before acting (ReSim) matched or beat much larger prompting baselines at about 2x tokens.
numbers: ReSim Sokoban 96.4+-0.2 vs R1 96.6+-0.2 (14.5x tokens); ALFWorld 87.7+-1.1 vs R1 62.5+-0.5; AndroidWorld 34.4+-0.4 vs Qwen2.5-VL-72B 19.5+-0.4.
limits: ReSim needs a rollout model, value function and aggregator; GPT-4o was judge on Android. Authors could not reproduce UI-TARS 1.5.
agent_relevance: Structured simulation beats longer free reasoning per token.

source: Dyna-Mind (2025) SimRollout prompting without training
finding: Prompted simulated rollouts help untrained models a little.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B Sokoban 25.8 to 30.0, ALFWorld 35.4 to 39.1. GPT-4o Sokoban 37.8 to 41.4, ALFWorld 51.3 to 64.8. GPT-4.1 Sokoban 67.9 to 71.1, ALFWorld 54.4 to 67.9.
limits: Single table; gains 3 to 14 points; no variance in my extract.
agent_relevance: Direct scaffold evidence: simulate-then-act prompting helps, most on ALFWorld.

source: Dyna-Mind (2025) simulation quality correlates with success
finding: An LLM judge scores simulation ability. Correlation with success is high for untrained models but drops after RL.
numbers: Sokoban r: Qwen-7B .64, V3 .81, R1 .96; after Dyna-GRPO .64. ALFWorld r: R1 .70; Dyna-GRPO .55. Judge: Qwen3-235B.
limits: Judge-dependent scores; correlational; r falls after RL, so simulation quality is not the only driver.
agent_relevance: Measure whether simulations are accurate, not only whether they exist.

source: Dyna-Mind (2025) source of reasoning traces for distillation
finding: Training on search-based traces beat distilling long reasoning from R1 on ALFWorld.
numbers: ALFWorld AVG: Distill(ReSim) 74.1 vs Distill(R1) 56.8 vs Distill(V3) 57.8. Sokoban AVG 63.7 vs 64.8 vs 41.8. R1 distill costs 24.0x tokens vs 2.0x.
limits: Stage 1 used only trajectories solved by all methods (207, 200, 128).
agent_relevance: Explicit simulation traces transfer better than verbose thinking.

source: Dyna-Think (2025) Synergizing reasoning, acting and world-model simulation: OSWorld
finding: On OSWorld (174 tasks), world-model training in Dyna style improved the 32B agent; naive Dyna did not help best-of-N.
numbers: Avg success: DIT(R1) 22.6+-1.0; +vanilla Dyna 24.1+-2.1 (BoN 29.3, down from 40.7); +DDT next-state 25.9+-1.4; +DDT critique 26.6+-1.5 (BoN 49.6). R1 31.2+-1.4 (BoN 48.8); GPT-4o 16.5+-2.5.
limits: 20,480-token context cap. 7B gave limited gains. Only 3 runs.
agent_relevance: Replay of simulated experience can hurt if the world model is poor; critique-style training is what helped.

source: Dyna-Think (2025) WindowsAgentArena and world-model accuracy
finding: Vanilla Dyna hurt on WindowsAgentArena; DDT helped. Better world-model accuracy tracked better policy.
numbers: WAA avg: Qwen-32B 23.9+-1.1; R1 26.9+-1.5; RFT 28.4+-1.8; vanilla Dyna 20.9+-1.1; DDT next-state 34.9+-1.4; DDT critique 32.8+-1.4. World-model accuracy: R1 53.1% (r=.37 with success), DIT(R1) 38.9% (r=.45), DDT critique 55.7% (r=.44).
limits: r about .4 is moderate. 703 synthetic trajectories raised BoN but not robustness.
agent_relevance: A bad simulator lowers performance below no simulation. Gate replay on simulator quality.

source: Dyna-Think (2025) abstract claim
finding: Abstract reports similar best-of-n to R1 with 2x fewer tokens on average.
numbers: 2x fewer tokens.
limits: Abstract only; numbers are in b22 and b23.
agent_relevance: Cost case for structured simulation.

source: DreamGym (2025) Scaling agent learning via experience synthesis
finding: A reasoning world model generates synthetic experience, with a replay buffer and generated tasks. Zero real data roughly matched real-data GRPO/PPO on WebShop and ALFWorld and beat them on WebArena.
numbers: WebShop Q2.5-7B: GRPO (80K real) 66.1; DreamGym 0 real 68.3; DreamGym-S2R (5K real) 72.1. ALFWorld Q2.5-7B: GRPO 79.8; DreamGym 71.0; S2R 82.4. WebArena Q2.5-7B: GRPO 6.1; DreamGym 12.7. Real transitions 80K vs 5K (about 6%).
limits: WebArena absolute rates are low (9 to 14.5%). Text claims over 30% but the table shows 9.1 to 14.5; unexplained. Single-environment setups. ALFWorld Llama-3.2-3B DreamGym 62.1 < GRPO 65.3.
agent_relevance: Offline synthetic experience can replace most real interaction, given a small real seed.

source: DreamGym (2025) ablation
finding: Every component matters: experience replay, reasoning in the world model, and task generation.
numbers: WebShop/WebArena: full 63.9/13.3; no replay 59.2/9.7; no reasoning 55.8/7.3; no task generation 57.3/7.3.
limits: Averages over models; no variance given.
agent_relevance: Replay buffer adds 4.7 and 3.6 points; reasoning in the simulator adds more.

source: Agent Learning via Early Experience (2025)
finding: Training agents on their own action outcomes (implicit world modelling, self-reflection) improved effectiveness and out-of-domain generalisation over expert-demo SFT in eight environments.
numbers: Eight environments, two strategies; the abstract gives no success figures.
limits: Only the abstract was read.
agent_relevance: Same direction: learn from self-generated outcomes offline.

source: Holt et al. (2025/2026) Fact-augmented lookahead planning for LLM agents
finding: In-context method that distils atomic facts after each episode and uses them for one-step world-model simulation and lookahead. Improves cumulative return over ReAct, Reflexion and search-only baselines on FrozenLake variants, CrafterMini, ALFWorld.
numbers: No figures on the abstract page. AISTATS 2026.
limits: Never calls itself Dyna. Numbers not read.
agent_relevance: A pure-prompt analogue of episode-end offline consolidation.

source: Sutton (1991) Dyna; Sutton and Barto Dyna-Q+ shortcut experiments
finding: Could not open the chapter (certificate error). Standard claim: Dyna-Q cannot find a new shortcut in a changed maze; Dyna-Q+ adds an exploration bonus to do so.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Background only.
agent_relevance: The Dyna-Q+ bonus maps to re-testing library entries untouched for long.
